title: the birth of the cousins
hook: in the forest, Kunti tells Pandu about a mantra a sage gave her as a girl, and three gods are called

segments.voice: Yesterday in the birth of the cousins: Pandu's arrow, Kindama's curse, and a king in the forest with no way to have sons. What did you pause before? Day seven hundred twenty-six.

Years before any of this, a girl named Kunti served a sage in her father's house. He was Durvasa, a sage hard to please, and she served him so carefully that, when he left, he gave her a gift: a mantra. With it, she could call any god she chose, and have a son by him. She has kept it quiet ever since. Now her husband sits in the forest, cursed, asking how his line can go on. And Kunti speaks.
screen: `A GIRL SERVES A SAGE.` → `A MANTRA, GIVEN.` → `KEPT QUIET FOR YEARS.`

segments.voice: Pandu raises it first. He tells Kunti of the old custom, the same one that brought him into the world through Vyasa, and asks her to have sons for him by a worthy man. Kunti answers with her secret: the mantra. Pandu is overjoyed. Which god first? He chooses Dharma, the god of righteousness, so the eldest son will be just. Kunti calls, and Dharma comes, and a son is born. A voice from the sky blesses the child, the text says, and he's named Yudhishthira. Then Pandu asks for a son of great strength. Kunti calls Vayu, the wind, and Bhima is born. The text tells a story to show what he is: as an infant, he tumbles from his mother's lap onto a mountain, and it's the rock that shatters. Then Pandu wants a son who'll be foremost among warriors. He keeps vows himself, and Kunti calls Indra, king of the gods. Arjuna is born, and again a voice from the sky speaks over him. Three sons: justice, strength, and skill. But notice what Kunti doesn't say. She tells Pandu about the mantra. She doesn't tell him everything about how she first learned what it could do. That piece waits for days ahead. Notice, too, that this story is shaped like the one we just finished. A line with no heir, a hidden gift from a sage, and a woman who finally speaks about it. Satyavati's secret saved the Kuru house once. Now Kunti's does the same, in the next generation. The cousins are arriving.
screen: `PANDU ASKS FOR SONS.` · `KUNTI'S MANTRA.` · `DHARMA, VAYU, INDRA.` · `WHAT KUNTI DOESN'T SAY.`

segments.voice: Sit easily, and let the breath find its pace. Pandu chose what he hoped his sons would carry: justice, strength, skill. Bring to mind someone younger you care about, a child, a niece, a student, a new colleague. What would you wish to grow in them? Let one quality come. Don't make it a plan. Just hold the wish, lightly, for a few breaths. If you pray, you might bring them into your prayer in your own way. The bell holds the time.
The birth of the cousins. Kunti's mantra calls Dharma, Vayu and Indra, and Yudhishthira, Bhima and Arjuna are born.
screen: `THE BIRTH OF THE COUSINS — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: the birth of the cousins. Today, tell one younger person a good quality you see growing in them. Day seven hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: In Hindu tradition, Indra is praised in Vedic hymns, Vayu is the wind and the breath, and Dharma is righteousness itself; in this story they become fathers of the Pandava brothers.

match.prompt: three sons, three gods — tap the pairs.

myth: it came from the sage Durvasa, whom she served as a girl.
baby Bhima fell onto a rock and the rock shattered
the text tells it to show his strength.
he chose Dharma first, so the eldest would be just.

fork.setup: you're Pandu. Kunti can call any god to give you a son. which do you choose first?
fork.reveal: he chooses Dharma, and Yudhishthira is born.

original.note: Sanskrit mantra: a sacred formula; Kunti's, from Durvasa, calls a god to give her a son.

trapdoor: what you thought: magic words that summon gods.
what it means: a gift earned by service and kept quiet until the family needs it.
what a scholar hears: the pattern of Satyavati's secret repeats in Kunti's, a generation on.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva (Pandu asks Kunti for offspring; Kunti's boon from Durvasa; the births of Yudhishthira, Bhima and Arjuna)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Pandu's appeal to the old custom; Kunti's account of Durvasa's boon; the order Dharma, Vayu, Indra; the voices from the sky at Yudhishthira's and Arjuna's births; infant Bhima falling and shattering the rock; Pandu's vows before Arjuna's birth.
No meaning is given for Yudhishthira's name, under the claims rule. Durvasa is called 'hard to please'; confirm against Ganguli's description.
Karna is deliberately not mentioned; 'she doesn't tell him everything' foreshadows 'Karna's abandonment' (days 728–733). Confirm Kunti's account to Pandu in Ganguli omits Karna.
Gandhari's sons and Madri's twins are left for day 727.
howItsDone generalizes about how Indra, Vayu and Dharma are honored; confirm phrasing.
Editor pass: open-hand image in the practice replaced (used on 712 and nearby); howItsDone generalization about how Hindus honor the gods softened.
